title: triple-sdk-call-surface-refactor-and-stable-backoff-presets
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Polish SDK call signatures across Python/TS/Go, add stable backoff presets and parity fixes; bump SDK minor versions (py 1.8.0, ts 2.3.1, go 1.5.0). No public API breaking changes expected for typical usage; migration notes included in changelogs.
description:
Motivation: Our tri-SDK ergonomics diverged again after incremental fixes to async streaming and auth rotation. This PR standardizes the call surface for generation/chat/stream APIs across Python, TypeScript, and Go, centralizes retry/backoff presets (optimistic, conservative, throughput-aware), and applies a set of parity fixes discovered during cross-SDK smoke tests. Summary of changes is below.

What changed (high level):
- Introduce a compact retry Preset registry (Presets: optimistic, balanced, conservative) implemented in each SDK with matching semantics and telemetry hooks.
- Harmonize streaming call signatures: stream responses now expose the same iterator/async iterator names, error shapes, and heartbeat/close semantics across languages. Python: AsyncGenerator compatible with 'aiter_tokens()' helper; TS: AsyncIterable with 'streamTokens()' helper; Go: channel-based StreamToken iterator with Close() symmetry.
- Centralize auth handshake behavior: SDKs will attempt soft-refresh once per request on token expiry error, using the same retry predicate and backoff window.
- Small ergonomics: unify parameter names (timeout -> deadline_ms internally; retry -> retry_preset), flatten nested options for common use cases, and provide explicit migration notes.
- Tests and examples: added crosslang smoke harness and three sample notebooks/apps demonstrating parity.

Why this is different: instead of only copying shapes, this refactor extracts the retry policy definitions into a language-agnostic spec in the repo (docs/sdk/retry-presets.md) and implements concise SDK adapters that match the spec so behavior is reproducible across environments and easier to maintain.

Checklist: 
- [x] Spec doc for retry presets and stream semantics (docs/sdk/retry-presets.md)
- [x] Python implementation and minor API shim for backwards compatibility (packages/python/redwood_sdk/*)
- [x] TypeScript implementation and deprecation warnings (packages/typescript/redwood-sdk/*)
- [x] Go implementation with examples (packages/go/redwood-sdk/*)
- [x] Crosslang smoke tests and CI matrix entry
- [x] Changelogs and migration notes

Commits summary: see commits field below for compact list.

Changed areas (high level):
- packages/python/redwood_sdk/core/retry.py (new Preset registry and telemetry hooks)
- packages/python/redwood_sdk/streaming/async_stream.py (stream adapter and iterator helpers)
- packages/typescript/redwood-sdk/src/retry/presets.ts (matching presets and typed docstrings)
- packages/typescript/redwood-sdk/src/stream/streamAdapter.ts (async iterable helpers)
- packages/go/redwood-sdk/internal/retry/presets.go (preset registry and tests)
- packages/go/redwood-sdk/stream/stream.go (StreamToken iterator and Close semantics)
- docs/sdk/retry-presets.md (spec + examples)
- examples/tri-sdk-stream-mirror/* (three example apps)
- tests/integration/sdk-parity/* (smoke harness)

Notes on compatibility: For most users the surface should be compatible; we preserved older helpers but added clear deprecation warnings in TS (console) and Python (warnings.warn). Go retains current constructor signatures but introduces an options flattening helper NewClientWithDefaults(opts) that is recommended. Migration notes are in packages/*/CHANGELOG.md.

Risk assessment and mitigations:
- Risk: subtle difference in error shapes from streaming layer. Mitigation: added a mapping layer per SDK that normalizes errors (see packages/*/stream/error_map.go|py|ts).
- Risk: flaky crosslang CI. Mitigation: smoke tests run in a separate matrix and have retry on infra flakiness; temporary allowlist for known ephemeral failures.

Manual testing performed: tri-sdk parity run against local staging model, smoke stream tests with long-lived connections (30m), token-expiry simulation and soft-refresh checks, and example apps executed end-to-end.

References: Linear ENG-1042, ENG-1108; incident notes SUP-3482 (auth rotation flakiness).

Maya Chen (author): Added re-export to src/index.ts and a short deprecation note in CHANGELOG.md. Tests updated to cover re-export consumers.
Liam O'Connor: Go Close() semantics look consistent, but please add a small note in docs about when Close() is required vs optional for latte-style consumers.
